utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. And good morning to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: May I remind you of the affirmation that you made which still applies as you continue with your evidence. Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Ali.

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you a few questions about the police station of Bit Pazar. Is that correct that while you stayed at the police station in Bit Pazar you were interviewed by a police officer who asked about your state of health. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall that this police officer who came to talk to you indicated that had you been arrested pursuant to an order of an investigative judge? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown 1D190, ERN 1D002133, the Macedonian is 1D002131. It's 1D190. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you have the document in front of you, Mr. Ali?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... At the top left-hand corner of the document you will see that it is a document that comes from the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Macedonia, department of the minister of the interior, Bit Pazar, and it's dated the 13th of August, 2001. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in this Official Note there's a comment or a note by a person named Saso who reads in the following terms: "On the 13 August 2001 at 2200 from the PS Kisela Voda upon the request of the PS Cair and verbal order of the investigative judge from the Basic Court Skopje II Beqir Shahini, the following persons were brought to be kept in the PS Bit Pazar. Then there's a list of name and the last name is yours, is that correct, number 4?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what the police officer in question comments is the following: "I searched the person and made visual inspection and I concluded that a physical force is used upon them, in other words, they have obvious bruises and their bodies and faces." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And does that refresh your memory about this meeting with the police officer at Bit Pazar?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is not true. No one asked us how we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you recall a police officer coming to you at Bit Pazar searching you and looking at your injuries? Is that something that you recall now?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the registry please turn to the next page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, in this note there is the following annotation or note. It says that on the 14th August 2001 verbal order of the investigative Judge Beqir Shahini from the Basic Court Skopje II from PS Kisela Voda into PS Bit Pazar were brought the following persons. And on the number 4 is your name again. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall a police officer indicated to you that you had been transferred from one police station to the other pursuant to an order of an investigative judge? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember. We went to the court after the Bit Pazar police station. After Bit Pazar, we were taken to the court at 2.00 a.m. in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't that correct, sir, that it wasn't the only the interview which you had. You also were interviewed or had meeting with police officer whilst you were at Kisela Voda police station. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown what is P53 with an ERN range ET-N001-9839-01. And the Macedonian version is P53, N001-9827-13.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ali, are you able to read that copy? It's not a very good quality. Are you able to read it?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's difficult to be read.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, I have a paper copy which is slightly better.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If I draw your attention, Mr. Ali, on the top left-hand corner again it's a document -- once again it's an Official Note and it again comes from the MVR, Ministry of Interior Republic of Macedonia, sector of interior, Skopje. It's submitted by someone called Deyan.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: As for the date, Your Honour, it mentions the 18th on the English version. We are not concern this is the correct date on the original. It could be the 13th.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, if I can draw your attention to the subject heading first of that document. It says that it is regarding the official interview conducted with persons who were undertaken from Ljuboten village. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the person Deyan went on to say this: "On 12 August 2001 in the premises of DOI Kisela Voda, department of interior, I had interviews with nine persons from Ljuboten village. There were apprehended by the associated security forces of the Republic of Macedonia in the time when combat actions were performed in the village. They were identified and later on through interviews and examination with these persons it was confirmed that these men are as follows." Then there's a list of name and in the middle of them there is your name, Ali Isni. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then it says the following: "It was confirmed that all of them, nine men, were presenting in Ljuboten village in the time when combat actions were performed by the security forces of Republic of Macdonia. When asked about the events happened in their village, they stated the following: Shots of weapon could be heard coming out from side of the village. Actually, combat activities were led between the police of the Republic of Macedonia and the terrorist gangs. The aforenamed persons stated that they noticed many terrorists fighting and were having fire-arms in their hands. Nevertheless, themselves, they didn't take part in the fights, said they. They wanted to run away from the village and some of them wanted to surrender to police as they did not take part in the fights." Do you recall saying that to the police officer, Mr. Ali?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is not true. And I don't know who can make up this kind of documents. None of them are true.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't that the truth, sir, that at the time that you and the other villagers were being truthful with the police and that later on it was agreed not to mention the NLA anymore. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question. Once again, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: To my or -- or my translation of this document doesn't mention the NLA. And the question just put by my learned colleague includes the NLA. Maybe my colleague can rephrase that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ali, is that correct that at the time you saw members of the NLA or otherwise armed men in the village. Is that correct? And I'm talking members of the NLA or Albanian armed men.

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is not true. There were no armed people in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't that correct that you and several over villagers told that fact to the police upon your arrest? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that also correct, Mr. Ali, that you and many other villagers later changed the story and stated there had been no members of the NLA and otherwise no armed Albanian fighters in the village? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true. The police didn't even ask us during the arrest. They didn't ask us and this is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then in your evidence in chief and in your statement, rather, you indicated that you were taken from Bit Pazar to Skopje Court. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Bit Pazar police station at 2.00 in the morning, we were taken to the Skopje Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in your evidence in chief you indicated that you had been subjected to abuse at the Skopje Court. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Including by a person who you understood to be a judge. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was a female judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that female judge suggested that you should be killed. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. She stepped on my own -- my toes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you -- it is your evidence that another judge forced you to sign a statement. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He forced me as a police --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And your lawyer did nothing. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have a lawyer.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And last week, or, sorry, I'm sorry, previously when you were here a few weeks ago, you were asked by the Prosecution who do you recall subjected you to mistreatment, and you indicated that they were reservists and active police officers. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what they were. There was a lot of policemen there. They are in hospitals, in prisons. They mistreated people, and when they would get sick, they were sent to the hospitals where they were mistreated again. They were mistreated in police stations and courts.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So is that correct, sir, that in fact you don't what category of police officers those individuals were a part of. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were all types of police officers. Reservists, regular policemen. All of them were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm asking you specifically about the people who you say inflicted treatment on you that day. Is that correct that as you've just stated you were -- you don't know what part of the police or what part of the police units they would be from. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know they were regular policemen, together with reservists. They had reservist uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct, sir, that you never mentioned either reservists or active police before giving evidence in this courtroom?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said there were all kinds of police officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that in your statement to the Office of the Prosecutor of 2003 you did not mention that they were reservists or active police officer. You simply mention that they were policemen who had mistreated you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were police officers. I said 100 times there were policemen and there were all kinds of policemen. In fact, there were active police officers and reservists.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But is that correct that you never mentioned the fact that you had identified those police officers as active policemen and reservists in your statement to the Prosecution in 2003. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have said police officers, in general, and in fact they are-- they were policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that also correct that in 2004 when you were interviewed a second time by the Prosecution you also only mentioned police officers. No mention of reservists or active policemen. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've said policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, again, in your addendum of the 26th of April of 2007 when you read back your previous statement you made no mention of active police or reservist police. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember if I have mentioned that or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that right, sir, that during your previous stay here in The Hague you met with your fellow villager, Mr. Mehmedi, Farush Mehmedi?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that also correct that you discussed your evidence with Mr. Mehmedi at that time?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So if Mr. Mehmedi were to say in this courtroom that you discussed your evidence with him, he would be a liar. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Or mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Or mistaken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Or confused. The proposition of a liar is that one that we have mentioned before as putting an unjustified singular position. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will rephrase the question for fairness purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ali, if Mr. Mehmedi had told this court - Your Honour, it's page 2.069 - that he had discussed his evidence with you while here in The Hague, he would have been either incorrect or would not have told the truth. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He hasn't -- he didn't tell the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if both you and Mr. Mehmedi had suddenly recalled or given evidence that the police officer in Skopje Court were members of the active and reservist police, that would be a coincidence, is that correct, is that your position?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The witness, Mr. Mettraux, has not at all acknowledged that he suddenly recalled. He has said that in previous statements he merely mentioned that they were police.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I withdraw the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Mehmedi -- Mr. Ali, I'm sorry, is that correct that were charged with a criminal offence of terrorism by the prosecutor? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, instead of going through the document and to speed up matter, I will simply identify the documents. It's P50, ETN-002-0138-1. And the indictment is P50-ET N002-0128-01.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that also correct, Mr. Ali, that you were detained pursuant to an order of the investigative judge at the Sutka prison. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct that subsequently your detention was prolonged on three other occasions. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct that neither you nor your lawyer challenged the prolongation of the detention which was ordered against you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll simply indicate the numbers. It is P50, ET N002-0230-01; P50, ET-N002-0283-1; P50, ET N002-0296-1; P50, ET N002-0307-1.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct, sir, that on each and every one of those occasion the court in Skopje found there was sufficient evidence to -- to continue your detention in the Sutka prison. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct, sir, that on the 14th of December of 2001 you were granted a presidential pardon and were released from prison?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that in that presidential pardon the president expressed a view that you had been a member of the ONA or LNA, as the document calls it. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is P50, ET N002-0332-1.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ali, is it correct that in March of 2002 you went again to Skopje Court?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is this about, because I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct that in March of 2002 you were called as a witness in relation to the death of your son. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we can see P55 with an ERN ET N002-1220-N002-1221-1. And the Macedonian version is N002-1146-074.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct, sir, that an investigative judge, Mr. Dragan Nikolovski asked you a question about the circumstances of the death of your son on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember this, but I don't think it's correct. The internationals were the ones who asked us about what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't that correct that on the 21st of March of 2002, Judge Nikolovski asked to you be provided by a certificate and a photo of your son Erxhan. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that they took a photograph and a birth certificate from me, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that also correct that Judge Nikolovski asked for your permission for an exhumation of the body of your son?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They asked for permission, but I don't know who exactly asked of this permission. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you see the document in front of you, Mr. Ali?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If we could please turn to the second page of that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, while we're waiting for that, is that correct that at that meeting you were accompanied, among other people, by Mr. Kenan Salievski or Saliu, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that you had also requested that representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal be present?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember this.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, if we can look at the top of this second page of the document, the record of the meeting, or hearing is as follows. It says: "In capacity of legal representative of the deceased, Erxhan Ali, one Isni Ali, legal representative, father of the deceased Erxhan is being questioned." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat it? I didn't understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It is the first paragraph on the top of the page. In the English it reads as follows: "In capacity of legal representative of the deceased, Erxhan Ali, one Isni Ali, legal representative, father of the deceased Erxhan, is being questioned. Can you see that at the top of the page?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then the second paragraph it says: "I'm the father of Erxhan Ali born 19/05/1996 in Skopje. I submit a certificate number 29.12.2/380, dated 21st March 2001. I also submit the photograph of little Erxhan Ali and I would like it returned to me once the procedure is over." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then there's a paragraph where you were asked question about Erxhan. And then it says: "I agree there an exhumation of the body of my son be performed." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you say: "I have nothing else to say. The minutes have been dictated out loud. I recognise them as my own and signed them myself." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then it takes notice of the fact that at the hearing the deputy public prosecutor Dragoljub Cakic, the investigative Judge Beqir Shahini, a representative of the municipal community of Ljuboten, Kenan Salievski, as well as a representative of The Hague Tribunal Andzei Sidlik and Ali Nakija from The Hague Tribunal were present." Do you see that. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you now recall that representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor were present on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know these persons, but they were both internationals and people from Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And whilst you were before the investigative judge Mr. Nikolovski did you raise a complaint against -- about what had happened to you in the police station at Bit Pazar and Kisela Voda?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was not possible for us to complain, because the document was ready, already prepared and we were just forced to sign it. They didn't asked us what happened to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you mean to say that you were forced to sign this very document which is in front of you right now?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where does this document come from?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, we have received it from the Office of the Prosecution, Mr. Ali.

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, but I really don't understand your question. Is it a document from the court or is it from the Bit Pazar police station or is it another document?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, first I would like you, if you can, to just answer the question before. You've indicated that you were forced to sign -- you were just forced to sign it. When you said that, Mr. Ali, were you referring to this particular document?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you saying, Mr. Ali, that you did not sign this document?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not saying that. I did sign it, but what is this document about?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Just, if you can, Mr. Ali, if you could just answer the simple question: Is that your evidence that you were forced to sign this document or not?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if you understand me, but I really cannot read this document. I don't know what this document refers to.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it because it is not clear on your screen, Mr. Ali, or is it something else? I have a paper copy perhaps, with the assistance of the court usher.

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ali, do you recognise your signature at the bottom of this document?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I signed this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that your evidence that you were forced -- forced to sign this document?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not this one. I willingly signed this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Going go back a few step to my earlier question, is that correct that you did not raise an issue with the investigative judge as to what you said happened to you at the Bit Pazar police station and Kisela Voda police station. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no possibility for us even to speak, let alone to file a complaint.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that your evidence, sir, that you were prevented to speak during the hearing with Judge Nikolovski on that occasion? Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which hearing are you referring to? Hearing in Macedonia or where? I really don't understand you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can I interrupt here. I see Mr. Neuner wanting to object, but let me have an observation first, Mr. Mettraux. You are at every material point pushing what the witness has said beyond what he has said and then casting a proposition. The witness is putting to you and has not had from you an answer whether this is a document from the court or from a police station. He said he signed it; he was not forced to sign it. But you have not explored with him then how or why he came to sign it and can he remember it was at court. And you jump past that to the proposition, are you saying you were not allowed to do certain things, et cetera. If you can just see that the witness's mind and your mind are not meeting. And therefore you're misunderstanding or putting to him things that I don't think he has really indicated yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ali, following His Honour Judge Parker's observation, do you recall, having read that document, having had a meeting at the court in Skopje with the persons indicated in the document, which we have just read? Do you recall that meeting?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall having a meeting with representative of the Prosecution and a prosecutor and an investigative judge where you gave a certificate and a picture of your son, Erxhan. Do you recall such a meeting?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall that it took place in Skopje at the court. Can you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you recall being asked questions by the investigative judge at that time about the death of your son and about the possibility of an exhumation. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And during that meeting, Mr. Ali, do you recall being prevented in any way to speak or to talk to the investigative judge?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we were not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct that during that meeting with the investigative judge you did not raise the issue of what you said had happened to you at Bit Pazar and Kisela Voda. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat it? Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that during the meeting with the investigative judge and the other people indicated in the document you did not raise the issue of what you said had happened to you at the Bit Pazar and Kisela Voda police station. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We couldn't speak and we couldn't file a complaint. It was the court who prepared these documents. They wrote in them whatever they wanted.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And when you say "we couldn't speak and we couldn't file a complaint," why was that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because we were beaten, we were almost dead. They threw water on us just to make it possible for us to gain consciousness again. And can we make a small break, because I cannot go on responding to these nonsense questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can also indicate that I will be finished in approximately less than five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can I say there that the way your -- your mind is working quite differently from the witness. He has jumped, as I hear him, to another occasion he was in court.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And therefore we're getting confusing evidence again. Mr. Ali, if I could point out to you that you may find some of this very confusing, but Mr. Mettraux has to try and understand what it is you are saying. The process may not be easy for to you follow, but we would ask you to try and cooperate and assist as much as you can. There is very little more of this to go, and I think you'll find it easier if it can be finished rather than have to come back and have more of it. So we'll just press on for a little longer. Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ali, I'm sorry if the question was not clear. I was not referring to a time-period earlier. I was referring to the meeting you had in March of 2002, the document which we have reviewed together. And my question concerning any complaint you could have made related to that particular meeting in March of 2002. Are you able to answer this question: Is that correct that you did not raise with the investigative judge on that occasion any of the matters relating to your treatment at the Bit Pazar and Kisela Voda police station. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which investigative judge and which document? This document before me is about Erxhan. Now you're mentioning Erxhan and then you're mentioning Bit Pazar police station. You're confusing me. I don't understand the question. This document pertains to Erxhan and I signed it wilfully. So I don't want else to add to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps my question was the problem. During this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think not, Mr. Mettraux. Can I indicate that the chamber understands fully the witness is saying, yes, I went to court at some time, and there I remember a judge and a prosecutor and we were dealing with the death of my son and I gave to the court the photograph and the birth certificate and I did sign this document. He is not suggesting that he said anything else and the document does not suggest he said anything else. I think you can --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- take it that that is the position.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ali, is that correct that you never filed any criminal charges in relation to the mistreatment which you described in your evidence in chief?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that also correct, sir, that on the 12th of August of 2001 a shell hit the roof of your house. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This happened on Sunday, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct that as a result of the hit your roof was seriously damaged. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct also that when you were released from detention your house had been repaired. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct that the reparation or the work done on your house had been done by members of your family?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct that you received no assistance for that work from an international organisation or reconstruction company. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We received some help.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall from whom you received that help, Mr. Ali?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember this, because I was in prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm grateful for your patience, Mr. Ali.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mettraux. Mr. Apostolski, are there any questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have some questions for it witness but considering the fact that this witness asked for a small break I'm wondering whether to start with my cross-examination or to make the break first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think you should start, Mr. Apostolski. I understood the witness to be confused by the questioning and I think we've got over that confusion. Is that right? Yes. Carry on, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness Ali Isni, my name is Antonio Apostolski and together with my colleague Jasmina Zivkovic, we represent Mr. Johan Tarculovski in these proceedings. First of all I would like to express my personal condolences and the condolences of my client Johan Tarculovski about the death of your son. You were born in Ljuboten and you live in this village. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You have completed primary school in your native language, Albanian. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: After that, you completed secondary school in civil construction in Skopje; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the Albanians have lived for centuries in those regions, in the region of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Though I'm not involved in politics, I know that we have lived there forever.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the Albanian people lives now in the territories of today's Albania, Kosovo, Macedonia, Montenegro and Greece?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know those issues. I have not completed any political school. I know that the Albanians live in this area, so Albania is Albania, Macedonia is Macedonia, Kosovo is Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the Albanians who live in Macedonia and beyond are a proud people, and the honour is the supreme value in their cultural tradition?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once again, I didn't understand the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the Albanians who live in Macedonia and beyond are proud people and the honour is the supreme value in their cultural tradition?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I don't understand very well, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the Albanians are loyal to their family and beyond?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the Albanians who live in Macedonia are proud to protect their women?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Protect them from what?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I would rephrase the question like this. Is it correct that in the Albanian culture, men are the ones who safeguard the integrity of the family?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Women have also their rights. Men and women are equal.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that in the core of the Albanian culture when someone gives their word of honour, or besa, it means that they have to live up to the besa?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct. When you give your word of honour to someone, you have to live up, not to betray him.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Would an Albanian ever break up that promise, the besa?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are many -- a lot of Albanians. Everyone has his own besa.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In 1987, you served a conscription military service in Raska and Belgrade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell me in which branch of the army you were serving?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was four months in the infantry, then I worked in my -- but I have been taught to work in a workshop.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Does it mean that it is correct that you were trained to handle infantry weapons?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the army, yes, I had a training in automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: On the 10th of August, 2001, the shelling of the village of Ljuboten started, shelling by the Macedonian security forces. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You were at your house, and you were able to see the location where the shelling came from, towards the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Friday, 8.00, when the shelling from the police started, I could see it only from the other side, and we entered into the basement until lunch-time. I don't know exactly what hour it was. After lunch, the shelling stopped and we went out to go to the field, and at about 5.00 when the -- my son was killed we entered again the basement and that -- this is what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you tell me how many shells fell there on the Friday, 10th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. If you were in the basement frightened, could you have counted shelling and could you be able to say how many shrapnels and with what hand the shrapnels were taken off? So if that was to happen to you, would you have been able to say all these things? I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I have asked you only whether you are able to tell me how many shells fell in the village of Ljuboten in the morning of the 8th of August. If you are able to answer that, please do so.

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not count the shells. Many shells fell, but I wasn't able to count them. How could we count them? We were with the family, with the children. We were trying to survive in the basements and not come out and count the shells.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I apologise. My question was about the 10th of August, so on page 24, line 20 should read "10th of August." On Saturday, the 11th of August, the shelling continued; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On Saturday, from the morning until lunch there were -- there was -- there were shellings. In the afternoon the shellings stopped until Sunday morning. And then on Sunday, the police entered the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You stated that you did not feel safe, so you decided to leave the village, is that correct, on Sunday, August 12?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On Sunday, at about 6.00 in the afternoon, we left the house and we went to Skopje. We -- and we arrived at the Kodra e Zaimit check-point. This is where the police apprehended us and all the things occurred as everybody knows already.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: When you started from your house towards Skopje, you saw near the road, walking by, you saw the body of Sulejman Bajrami lying down on the street. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown the Exhibit P00019.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell me, can you recognise Sulejman Bajrami in this picture, in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He was killed here on this place -- spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell me at what time did you pass by his body on Sunday?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At about 6.00. We went here, above, and I saw -- I saw him from the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: We're speaking about 6.00 in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the afternoon. At about 6.00. I don't know the exact time.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Was his body at this location when you were passing by?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He was closer to the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I ask for the assistance of the usher to help the witness mark the location where he has seen the body of Sulejman Bajrami.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: If you could circle that in the photograph the location where the body of Sulejman Bajrami was lying?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please use an arrow to show where his feet were facing. Would this circle be his head?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This way. And I didn't have really time to see how his -- where was his foot or where were his fingers. I didn't get very close to see whether he -- where was exactly his finger. My family was behind me.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please mark with number 1 the place where the feet of the body were; and with the number 2 the location of the head.

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The head was here; his feet were on this side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could I just note for the record that number 1 depicts the head and number 2 the feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you see any other body, apart from the body of Sulejman Bajrami immediately next to his?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, there was no other body.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So if anyone else were to state before this Court that next to the body of Sulejman Bajrami there was another body, it would not be correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: A little further to the -- to the door of Sabri Ahmeti was lying the body of Muharon Bajrami, 20 to 30 metres further and here, next to Sulejman Bajrami there was no one. He was alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So the body of Bajrami -- I apologise. So the body of Ahmeti was near the door, 20 to 30 metres away from the body of Sulejman Bajrami?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Nearer toward the door. He is just indicating the direction, not the position of the body. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: They were 20 or 30 yards -- or metres apart, which I think is the point you're interested in.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I wish to tender this photograph in evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you want me to explain this again?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think we've grasped it enough, thank you. The photograph will be received as an exhibit. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be exhibit number 2D32.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: When asked by my learned colleague, the Prosecutor, you stated that when you testified before the investigating judge in Basic Court Skopje II, the judge who was interviewing you was stepping on your feet and he threatened you that unless you signed the statement he would call the police to beat you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: He or she, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It would be a he.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The judge in the -- during the trial was male. And in the corridor when the police was keeping there this -- a woman came there. She was in civilian clothes. I don't know if she was judge or what she was. She was the one who stepped on our toes. We were already dead. We could -- barely were able to breathe.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And the judge who took the statement from you, did he threaten you to sign the statement?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I -- he -- I asked him who wrote this, and he said, Just sign this, because I will bring in the police and they will beat you up.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You stated that you are able to recognise the judge; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you describe him. How did the investigating judge look?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had curled hair. He had about 30 to 35 years. He -- Beqir who was also in Ljuboten knows him because when we went to court for my son, Beqir and some foreigners that were there, that judge opened the door. When he saw me he just closed the door and I told to Beqir, This is the one, this is the judge that forced us to sign the documents. So Beqir know this is judge as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Are you now speaking about Beqir, the investigating judge in Basic Court Skopje II Beqir Shahini?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Beqir Shahini was there when weapon went to court for Erxhan and when this other judge came to this room, he immediately closed the door and he left and this is when I told Beqir that this was the judge who was there that night and who forced us to sign the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Apostolski. Mr. Neuner, is there any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Just a very few questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think Mr. Ali will be glad when you finish those very few questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: First I would have a question to my colleague Mr. Mettraux. The document 1D190, was this tendered by you? It's an Official Note 936 from Bit Pazar police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, did I not seek to tender this document for the reason that the witness had not acknowledged or remembered the meeting in question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to -- good morning, Mr. Ali. I want to take to you Friday afternoon, the 10th of August, 2001. You stated until about 5.00 you have been in the field, right?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On Friday, yes, when my son was killed, I was there going to the field and when the shell fell, it fell about 200 metres away from us, and I turned back and I went to my uncle Avdil.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And I think you also stated that you have been in the basement from that time onwards; after 5.00, so to speak?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In my uncle's house and it is there that my wife called and she said come back home because Erxhan was killed. And I could not get out of the basement. However, I was lucky, because I somehow came out of the basement and I went to my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And that day how long did you stay in the basement?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which basement?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You mentioned that on Friday after 5.00 you have been in the basement, and I just wanted to ask how long that day you have been in the basement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: He has spoken of more than one basement. I think he is saying that when there was an explosion in which his son was killed he went first to the basement of his uncle's house.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of my uncle's house basement, I stayed there about 15 minutes. After I called at -- I called my house, my wife responded and she said come quickly because our son was killed, and I went there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: That afternoon/evening, had you ever been to the school in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to take to you Monday, the 13th of August, 2001. You were at Bit Pazar police station?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know, Bit Pazar or Prolece station. I don't know. At that time I don't recall anything. What I recall is that I was at a police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And in what state of health had you been on Monday?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were -- we didn't know anything. We hadn't had anything to eat. Since my son was killed, I didn't even eat until we were taken to Sutka, I don't know how many days we were kept.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Ali, will you be pleased to know that --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- the questions that will be asked of you, the Chamber is very grateful that you have been able to come to assist us, and we know it's been difficult for to you try and have to think back over the details of those events, especially the death of your son. We thank you very much, and we indicate, of course, that you can now return to your home and your family.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, can I only make some questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I want to ask these people here why they killed Erxhan. He was only a child. He was playing on the street. He called him a terrorist. They traumatised my family. They killed my son. They destroyed my health. They put me to prison. This was done by Mr. Ljube Boskoski with his police and with the army of the Republic of Macedonia. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You'll understand that the answer to that question is one of the things that the three Judges here are looking at to see if they can find an answer, so that you'll just have to wait until we have finished hearing all the people who can help us with their evidence about what occurred and we then may have some answers to these problems that concern you. So thank you again. We now adjourn --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. Would you please read aloud the affirmation on the card given to you now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. The Prosecution will call witness Qamuran Rexhepi. Just, Your Honours, a brief issue. This witness has only one statement but it was certified twice due to an oversight. So we will seek to tender the first statement which was, sorry, the statement which was certified in 2005.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Rexhepi, good morning.

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Rexhepi, do you recall providing a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor in 2004?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Do you recall meeting with an officer appointed by your registry of this Tribunal to certify your statement in 2005?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Do you recall introducing some handwritten changes at that time?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Do you recall meeting with a colleague of mine in Ljuboten this year, and also with myself yesterday and introducing some further corrections?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: In particular, Mr. Rexhepi, do you recall indicating that in paragraph 2 of your statement you did your military service from 1994 to 1995?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did you also indicate that in paragraph 4 the man that you saw coming from above the hills was two to three kilometres closer to the village and you were not sure whether he was wearing a uniform because it was too far away?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Do you recall also indicating in paragraph 8 that the sentence: "We could see five men in camouflage uniform," should be replaced by "I could see approximately five men in camouflage uniform."

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Rexhepi, including these corrections that you made, are you satisfied that the statement that you gave is correct and accurate?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will seek to tender this witness's statement pursuant to Rule 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be exhibit number P372.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: The witness, Qamuran Rexhepi is a Ljuboten resident of Albanian ethnicity. On Friday, 10 August, 2001, the witness heard and saw shooting and shelling coming from the Macedonian positions above the hill. He also saw fighting coming from the church, from around the church and from the Brace's house where a police check-point was located. On Sunday, the 12th he saw a number of houses on fire in Ljuboten. He also saw approximately five men in camouflage uniform carrying gasoline and gas cylinders to set property on fire. Soon afterwards the witness and his family joined a large number of other villager who were fleeing Ljuboten. Once they arrived at the check-point, the police separated men from women. The men were forced to lie on the ground and they were beaten and mistreated. They were then transported by a police jeep to Butel or Cair police station and afterwards to Karpos police station where they were beaten and mistreated. At Karpos the witness undertook the paraffin test. On 14 August the witness was taken to Skopje Court. He saw how fellow villagers were beaten by police officers. He was then taken to Sutka prison where he remained for more than four months. Could I please call ERN N004-4729. It's 65 ter 199.22, page 290. It's photo A of page 9 of the court binder, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Rexhepi, in paragraph 3 of your statement you mention that on Friday you saw shooting from around a church. Are you able to see the church, the church in this photo, and, if so, could you please encircle it and write number 1.

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And write number 1, please.

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: For the record the witness has just drew a circle in the upper left side of the photo. Also in the same paragraph, you mention that you saw shooting coming from the Brace's house. Are you able to see the Brace's house in this photo, Mr. Rexhepi?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: The house cannot be seen here.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you please draw an arrow indicating the direction where the Brace's house is located?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: It's in the direction of Ljubanci village.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you please -- thanks. Could you please draw an arrow.

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Yes, yes. [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: For the record the witness drew an arrow on the right side of the photo. From this location how far would you say that the Brace's house is located?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: There is a road here. From this house up to there, it's about 10 to 15 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you please write then "10/15 metres," just above the arrow? That's okay.

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Rexhepi, are you able to see Rami Jusufi's house in this map -- sorry, in this photo?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you please encircle it and write number 3.

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you please write number 3 a bit more on the right side of the circle, because we cannot see the number. For the record the witness has just drew a circle on the left side of the photo in the centre part.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to exhibit this photo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be exhibit number P373.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could I please have display ERN N005-7603. It's the panoramic photo in the page 5 of your court binder. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Rexhepi, you mentioned in paragraph 8 of your statement that in the morning of the Sunday, the 12th, you saw approximately five men in camouflage uniforms carrying gasoline and gas cylinder.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If I could have the usher's assistance again. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If you could encircle the area where you saw these men and write number one.

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks. For the record the witness has drawn a circle just on the middle of the photo on the left of the mosque. Also in paragraph 8 and 9 of your statement you explain that your house --

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Excuse me. They were not at the church. They were behind my house.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: No. We understood, Mr. Rexhepi. I was just explaining for the record that you drew a circle on this photograph just behind the mosque that we can see --

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, behind the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks. Also in paragraph 8 and 9 of your statement you explained that the same morning, afterwards your house was set on fire. Are you able to see your house and drew a circle and write number 2?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: I marked my house with number 1. It's near the mosque, my house.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And you saw the men in camouflage uniform near your house?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Behind my house. The house that they burned down, I saw them behind that house, in the yard of Harun Rexhepi.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: For -- Mr. Rexhepi, the house of Harun Rexhepi, how close is to your house?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Just one metre apart. They're all together, the three houses that were burnt down, they were all close to each other. Harun's house, my house, and my uncle's house.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Can we agree then that within the circle and the number 1 you also mark your house and you also indicated Harun's house? Everything is in the same area?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: You also mention in paragraph 8 of your statement that Sunday morning near the church you saw the houses of Qenan Rashiti, Isuf Rashiti, and Sabit Rashiti burning. Are you able to see the house of Qenan Rashiti in this photo?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: I cannot find it. I cannot recognise it on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Do you think that if we make the photo bigger, you will be able to see it?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, can I exhibit this photo and then maybe we can have another still with a zoom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be exhibit number P374.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And, yeah, if we could call the same photo.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Rexhepi, would you like us to move a bit to the right or is this okay?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: You cannot see the house itself because there are other houses just in front of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Okay. So could you please simply drew an arrow where --

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yeah, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: -- indicating where the house is located of Qenan Rashiti?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: His house is behind these white houses that you see here.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Would you please write number 1.

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: You are able to see the house of Isuf Rashiti?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: I can only see the roof.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Okay. Could you please mark number 2.

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And, finally, can you see the house of Sabit Rashiti?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And write number 3. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: For the record, the witness has marked three houses which are a bit on the centre of the photo on the right side. Your Honours, I would like to exhibit this still.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be exhibit number P375.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And now, I'd like the help of Ms. Walpita because we will use a clip through Sanction. It's 65 ter 309, V000-3494. And the clip, it from 46 seconds until 1 minute, 3 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Rexhepi, you mention in paragraph 13 of your statement that you left Ljuboten together with your family and approximately 100 other villagers. Does this clip reflect those moments?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: On the 12th of August, it was a Sunday when we left the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Correct. And does this video capture those moments when you were leaving on Sunday, the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: How far is the location that we saw in the clip from the check-point where you were stopped approximately?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: I would say a half an hour away.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And that in kilometres? Are you able to be more accurate?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: About one kilometre to one and a half, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will seek to tender this clip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be exhibit number P376.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could I please call ERN N004-5084. It's the photo A depicted in the page 20 of the court binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And, Mr. Rexhepi, in the meantime we see this photo I would like to ask you when you were actually in the check-point and you were forced to lie on the ground facing the floor and you were mistreated, did the police say something to you?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you explain to the Trial Chamber what they say to you?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: They were cursing us at the check-point. They maltreated us, beated us. They did with us whatever they wanted.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did they use any weapon in particular to threaten you?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: I was holding my child in my arms, and I wanted to give my child to my wife, and he prepared his gun to shoot. He wanted to shoot at a two and a half month old baby. Then my wife came and picked the baby. They made us lie down, take off our T-shirts. They started to beat us. They were running on our backs. They were hitting us with whatever they could land their hands on, with weapons and whatever.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we could see now the photo. Mr. Rexhepi, do you recognise the photo -- the building depicted in this photo?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: This is the Karpos police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Is this the police station where you were taken by the police in the afternoon of Sunday, 12 August 2001?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Yes. After Butel. After Butel, we were taken to Karpos police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, could I exhibit this photo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be exhibit number P377.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could I please call Exhibit P00050, page 22, ERN N002-0205. That's not the document. It's 0205, N002-0205, not 0105.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: In the meantime that we wait for the document, Mr. Rexhepi, could I ask you a further question. When you were taken to Skopje Court, you mention in paragraph 32 of your statement that you saw fellow villagers being brought and beaten by police officer. Do you remember which type of uniforms were these police officers wearing in the Skopje Court?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: They were wearing camouflage uniforms. These were policemens and inspector from the Bit Pazar police station. They work as such even nowadays. They had the same uniform then, and I was severely beaten, so I could not recognise the colours, but they were camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And how did you know that they were from Bit Pazar?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Because one of the policemen who was standing by me when others tried to beat me said to them, "Stop, he is my client. Don't beat him." I know some of them. I saw them one or two weeks before I came here.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we move now to the document that you can see on your screen. You can see the Macedonian version on the right side.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: This document reads on the upper left corner: "Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Macedonia, and then it's dated 14 August, 2001, Skopje. The title is Official Note, 538 and the subject is official conversation conducted with persons taken over from the village of Ljuboten. The document reads: "On 12 August 2001, in Kisela Voda and in Karpos I conducted an official conversation with eight persons taken from Ljuboten." And if we see -- we move three lines below we see your name. In the next paragraph we can read: "From the conversations conducted with these persons they stated that shooting from all sides could be heard in the village, that is to say, that the persons so combating between the police and terrorist groups." In the next paragraph we can see: "They had also noticed several terrorists shooting from weapons." Mr. Rexhepi, were you interview in Karpos police station?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Although you were not interviewed, did you see the police fighting against anyone between -- excuse me, on Sunday, the 12th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: The police was firing at the civilians.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did you see during that weekend, 10 to 12 August, any NLA presence in the village?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: No, there weren't any.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Rexhepi, during the time that you were in Sutka and after you left Sutka were you ever contacted by any member of the police or the ministry of interior inquiring what had happened to you or what had happened in the Ljuboten the weekend 10 to 12 August 2001?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: No, no, nobody came to ask.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Qamuran Rexhepi. My name is Edina Residovic and together with my colleague Guenael Mettraux, I represent Mr. Ljube Boskoski before this trial. Before I start asking you some questions, Mr. Rexhepi, I would kindly ask you to carefully listen to my questions, observe a pause for the question to be translated, and only afterwards answer my question so that the interpreters would be in a situation, in position to translate my questions and your answers. Did you understand me, Mr. Rexhepi?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters kindly ask for Ms. Regue to turn off her microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Rexhepi, that in 2001 you and your family lived in Ljuboten; that is, you lived with your wife and your newly born son?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you can testify before this Court that Ljuboten is located not far from Skopje and that it is situated on the slopes Skopska Crna Gora Mountain. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also know probably that Skopska Crna Gora has exceptional strategic importance for the defence of the capital of Republic of Macedonia, Skopje; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My question is: Is it correct that the security of Skopje as a capital of the Republic of Macedonia is related for the security and safety of everything that takes place at Skopska Crna Gora. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: I don't understand the question at all. I don't understand what she's saying.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Maybe we will come at that issue in another way. You know that one could arrive across the slopes of Skopska Crna Gora Mountain to the border with Kosovo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Yes, there is a mountain. It can be crossed. I don't know what is the question exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You understood the question and you answered it. Is it also correct that on the other side of the Skopska Crna Gora mountain is the region of Kumanovo that borders with southern Serbia?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Considering the proximity to the borders of southern Serbia and Kosovo, that region is of importance for the safety of the capital and the entire state, the Republic of Macedonia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You know that in 2001 there was a crisis in the Republic of Macedonia and that in several areas, especially in those around the Kumanovo and Tetovo, there were open clashes before the terrorist groups and the army and the police of the Republic of Macedonia. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: No. In my village there were none. I'm not interested what was there in Kumanovo.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Because of that situation in the Republic of Macedonia, did you know that the command for the defence of the city of Skopje was established in order to prevent the penetration of the terrorist groups towards the capital?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In June 2001, the army of the Republic of Macedonia has deployed its forces also in the area of Skopska Crna Gora and in positions around the village of Ljuboten. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Once again, please more precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
