utterances.text: Are you aware that in June 2001, the army of the Republic of Macedonia deployed its forces in the area of Skopska Crna Gora and particularly in the region around the village of Ljuboten? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: A month before or I don't know exactly, maybe a month or two earlier, Ljuboten was surrounded by police. I don't know anything more than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement to the Prosecutor of this Tribunal, on the 4th of October, 2004, you stated to the best of your recollection and you spoke truthfully; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Once again, I didn't understand well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you were giving a statement to the investigator of the ICTY in 2004, did you speak the truth about the issues you were testifying about?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Then in item 3 of your statement you stated that on the 10th of August, 2001, from the positions of -- at Malistena the shelling of Ljuboten started. Do you remember that you testified about that?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: First shelling started from Malistena, which was a check-point above the village. This is where -- from where the shelling started.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you knew that those were the positions of the army of the Republic of Macedonia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: I came to know this from the villagers after the war that this was the army. I don't know whether it was the police or the army. I only know that the shelling came from above.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that place from where you saw the shelling started, as you testified, was at the distance of two or three kilometres from you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, the witness didn't say that exactly in his statement. Ms. Residovic, I think that in fairness to the witness that should be put into context. He said that he saw a man, in another paragraph he mentioned that he saw a man coming with a grenade two to three kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I apologise. The exact sentence was, and I apologise if I misinterpreted it. The witness just stated what was in his response, I don't know whether those were civilians, policemen, or anyone from the army, but I suppose that they were not soldiers, because their positions were outside of the village and probably from this context that they were outside of the village I probably interpreted it differently, thinking that the witness knew that it was exactly at those positions above the village the army was located. So I apologise, Your Honours, and it was not my intention to put to the witness something that he hadn't said.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rexhepi, you just stated now that you learned from your fellow villagers about this after the event. Is it correct that the information about the positions of the army around the village came also from the shepherds that were taking their sheep to pasture in that area?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: I want the question to be stated more clearly, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Rexhepi, that the information about the positions of the army around the village of Ljuboten would come to you from the village shepherds who took their sheep to pasture at the slopes around the village?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Rexhepi, that already in the spring --

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: I don't understand the questions. I want them more clearly. No one could go to the mountain a month or two earlier because when the police blocked this area neither the shepherds nor anyone else could go there because of the police or the army, whatever. I don't know who they were. They know for themselves those that were there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Although your answer did not make into the transcript, you just repeated your answer providing more detail so it is not necessary for me to repeat the question that I have asked earlier. With regards to what you have just stated, you said that the shepherds could not go into the mountain since they would have been stopped. Could you tell me precisely who was stopping the shepherds who took the sheep into the mountain?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: The police.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you state for the Court where exactly were the positions of the police who stopped and prevented the shepherds from going up into the mountain? Could you answer the question that I have asked you, please?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Please repeat it again.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Considering that you stated that the police or the army would stop the shepherds who took the sheep into the mountain, what I'm asking you is: Can you say where at the mountain were the positions of the police of the Republic of Macedonia? Where were their check-points?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: On the side of the Rastak village, on the east. Call them the valleys of Dina.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And on the road towards the mountains, the words Bacila and the Bel Kamen localities, can you tell me where were those police check-points?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: This is the point where they were, the valleys of Dina. The Bel Kamen was further than this spot. I'm not a shepherd. I didn't take sheep to the pasture to know exactly the place.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's move, then, to some different questions. Is it correct that already in the spring of 2001 a number of youngsters from the village of Ljuboten joined the NLA?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if I say that in the summer of 2001 around 20 people from Ljuboten have actively joined the ranks of the NLA, then it would be the truth; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if I were to put to you that many of the inhabitants of Ljuboten have actively helped the NLA, providing logistics support, then that fact would be correct. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if I were to tell you that Ljuboten was used as early as from the spring of 2001 as a logistics base of sorts for the NLA and that the weapons and food were transported through Ljuboten to Matejce and other places where fights of the NLA took place, it would also be correct. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You know Kenan Salievski. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: I know him as a fellow villager, as a friend.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in 2001 he was the president of the crisis committee in the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: I don't know this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if I tell you that Mr. Kenan Salievski in his statement to the Prosecutor of the ICTY enumerated many people who were NLA members, then you can agree with me that Kenan Salievski would know about those facts better than you do?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You are aware that on the 10th of August, the Friday, not far from Ljuboten at Ljubotenski Bacila locality, NLA planted mines that killed eight soldiers of the army of the Republic of Macedonia and that several soldiers were wounded. You must be aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Once again, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that on 10th of August, in the morning, the NLA planted a mine at Ljubotenski Bacila locality not far from the village of Ljuboten and that that mine killed eight members of the army and injured many other soldiers. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: The mine was planted four to five kilometres away from the village and the mine was not planted by the people of the NLA. I don't know who planted that mine there. It is not true that NLA people planted the mine there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you certainly know that on that day three armed persons who participated in the planting of that mine entered the village. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that among those persons there was also a Shefajet Bajrami, nickname Shef, who was otherwise a NLA member; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before this mine explosion at Ljubotenski Bacila the crisis committee organised guards or watches in the village, so that nobody who was uninvited could enter the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: No, there were no guards. No one guarded Ljuboten from the villagers. It is the police that guarded us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After the mine explosion on Friday, August 10, many of the villagers of Ljuboten, fearing that the fights in the city would be continued had left the village and moved towards Skopje. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Maybe someone had left the village. The village is big. I don't know. I could not stop the people from leaving.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you are you aware that the reasons why some people left the village was actually the fact that armed persons entered the village after the mine explosion?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Which persons do you refer to?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I have asked you a moment ago whether you were aware that after the mine explosion three armed persons entered the village, and my question pertains to those persons.

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: No, this is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement -- I apologise, before that, you and your family remained in the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement of 4th of October, 2004, you stated the following: "Sometime later in the afternoon, the Macedonian army started to shell from their positions on the hills. I came with some friends,, Samedin Rexhepi, Veap Aliu, and Erhan Aliu to the house of Avdil Aliu in the upper part of Ljuboten to see what was going on." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So when you were giving that statement on the 4th of October, 2004, you knew that in the hills above the village the positions of the Macedonian army were located; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And it would be different from what you explained a moment ago, that you did not know who was around the village, whether it was the army, the police, or someone else? Is that different from what you stated a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: After the war, I came to know who was there; but before the war, before the 12th of August, I didn't know who was there. This is what I said before. So I am speaking before the events in Ljuboten. Before the events, I didn't know; after that, I came to know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But in the statement that you gave to the Prosecutor on the 4th of October, 2004, you did not say that you -- that regarding those facts that it was the army positions above the village, you learned only after the conflict. But you stated instead that in the afternoon the army started shelling from the position above the village. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: The shelling was on Friday, from Malistena, from the check-point. I cannot make -- I could not make at the time a distinction from that distance whether it was police, army, or civilians. How can I tell that?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My question was very brief. I have just read that you stated in the item 4 of your statement, and it does not correspond entirely to what you have stated now. You stated earlier that the shelling started from the positions of the Macedonian army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, please, how far were you from the place where the shelling started from, from the positions of the Macedonian army?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: The check-point?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will read again to you what you have stated. "[In English] Sometime in the afternoon the Macedonian army starting to shell from their position on the hills. I went with my -- with some friends, Samedin Rexhepi, Veap Aliu, and Erhan Aliu to the house of Avdil Ali, house to the upper part of the Ljuboten to see what was going on." [Interpretation] So my question now is: How far were you from the location where the shelling of the village started from?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: The shellings were two to three kilometres away from the road that goes to the check-point to Malistena. As the crow flies it's -- I don't know exactly. I didn't have anything to measure the distance with.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you agree with me that this is a rather longer distance?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: If you go by the road, the distance -- it is far. The distance is large. But as the crow flies, the distance is shorter. We usually take the Ljubanci road to get there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the moment when you saw the shelling starting from the positions of the Macedonian army, neither you nor friends, Samedin Rexhepi, Veap Aliu and Erhan Aliu, had any binoculars with you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement that you gave to the Prosecutor in 2004 you stated that you saw a uniformed man coming from the positions of the army above the village and coming ten metres closer to the village and shooting from a hand-grenade launcher towards you. Do you remember stating this?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the additions to the statement that you gave to the Prosecutor on the 5th of June, you stated that you saw a man shooting from hand-grenade launcher but you could not see whether he was wearing a uniform, considering that he was at quite a distance; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: I -- what I said was correct. He was far, I couldn't see very well. The interpreters might have wrote that way.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you will agree with me that at such a distance it would have been difficult for you to notice what the person held in his hands; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: I haven't used arms, but he must have shot with something. He must have had something in his hand, since he was shooting.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So when you said that the person shot from a hand-held rocket launcher, you actually did not see at all what was the person shooting from, because from that distance you could not see the object that the person would be shooting from; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Once again, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement, and later in the additions and changes that you gave to the Prosecutor, you stated that you saw that the person was shooting from a hand-held rocket launcher. I'm putting to you that considering the distance from which you were watching, you could not see at all what was that person shooting with.

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: It is true that he shot. I don't know what he had in his hands. You are saying "hand-held launchers." I don't know what kind of hand-held launcher it was, but I know that the shell fell near to the place we were. I could not see exactly what kind of uniform he was wearing, whether he was a member of the army or the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So if I understood you well, because of the fact that a grenade fell, it was only your conjecture that the person was shooting with a hand-held grenade launcher while you actually did not see the actual person shooting; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You stated that the shooting on the 10th of August started very early, early in the morning. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you be more precise and say at what time the shooting started on that morning?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: I don't know the exact hour. No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You did not know that when you were giving your statement to the Prosecutor in October 2004. Did you know that or not?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A mistake. In October 2004 and not 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, where were you on Saturday, August 11, 2001?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: At home.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you recall whether there was shelling on that date and from which positions, if any?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: The shellings had stopped a little bit. There were no such intense shellings on Saturday, as far as I heard and saw while I was sitting in the basement at home.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And on Sunday, August 12th, you stated that you and 15 members of your family were together in the same house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you say when the shelling started on Sunday morning?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: At about 8.00, 7.30. The police started shooting from Ljubanci at the Meze Mahalla, the Meze area.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, Mr. Rexhepi, how far is your house where you were located from the church in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: As the crow flies, maybe 300, 400, 500 metres. I don't know exactly. Maybe less. 200 to 300 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At a given moment you testified that you saw and you felt smoke, because of which your father went outside to see what was taking place; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Yes, we went out together.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you and your father went out together to see what was going on; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: What time do you refer to? Once again, if you can, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Sunday morning. At one point in time, as you stated, smell of fire and smoke was felt, and then I asked you is it correct that your father then went out to see what was going on, and your answer was that you went out together, with your father, to see what was going on. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you went out immediately, both you and your father, to see what was going on outside; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Because behind the house was burning. There was a smell of smoke. This is why we went out to see what was happening.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So your father did not go out alone. He went out together with you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: He went out first and then I went out. We took some water to -- to try to put down the fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also testified that you saw then some people who were wearing masks and who were carrying automatic weapons but were also carrying --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: -- those gas tanks or these cylinders containing gas, those containers, did you see that?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: I have seen them when we went out to extinguish the fire. They were quarrelling among each other. I couldn't see what was that gas can or an automatic rifle or I don't know what he had. I just saw that there was fire bursting so it was not set on fire with a lighter. It was set on fire with something that would put the fire much quicker.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you described in detail that you saw one of those people throwing that cylinder and setting it on fire on to the grass. So the stable of Harun Rexhepi started burning immediately. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: First, our house was burned, not Harun's house.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, maybe this would be the convenient time to take the recess.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We can do that now. Do we understand that you will finish this afternoon and in time for the other counsel to finish with this witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope that I will finish in half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That will leave only quarter an hour for Mr. Apostolski and Ms. Regue. So can you please look carefully in the break to be quicker. Thank you. We will resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, before I proceed with my cross-examination, I would like to address you with the following. On page 48, lines 3 and 4, I apologised for the mistake I had made by erroneously stating certain facts. It is not a problem for me to apologise every time I make a mistake, and it is never my intention to state the facts in a document erroneously. However…I’m sorry, I’m being told that the interpretation is not correct. What I want to say is that I will always apologise both to the Court and the witness if I misquote something, and that it is never my intention to misquote. However, when I checked the transcript and the statement, I realised that, this time, I had quoted the witness correctly; the only mistake I made was when I said that he had stated that in paragraph 3, instead of paragraph 4 of his statement. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rexhepi, you probably remember that we spoke about how you saw the first houses that were burning in the village. We spoke about this before the break. In the statement you gave to the OTP, you said that the persons who carried these cylinders at one moment and, and I quote ,"[In English] ... the men putting all of these gas cylinders into a place where lots of hay had been collected by the village people. The men opened the valve of the cylinder, set it on fire and then threw it to the hay that immediately start to burn. That hay belonged to Harun Rexhepi." Do you remember saying this in your statement? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Harun's house was not burned. My house, our house was burned. Harun's house was burned later. I don't understand what you're putting to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: During the preparations for your testimony you told the Prosecutor "[In English] ... Rexhepi house after it had been burned down. I didn't actually see this house burning on 12th August 2001." [Interpretation] Did you say this?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. Could you please clarify.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the preparations for your testimony yesterday, you told the Prosecutor exactly what I just read out to you. That in fact you did not see on the 12th of August, 2001 Harun's house burned down and that you learned about this later after you were released. Did you say this yesterday to the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Harun's house was burned after our house was burned, when I was released. Actually, while I was still in prison, I found out that Harun's house was also burned down.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In fact, you didn't see with your own eyes how these policemen set these houses on fire; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: I saw them setting my house on fire. They were cursing in the Macedonian language. They were shouting. And when we went out to put the fire down, we heard this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that later on with 100 other inhabitants of Ljuboten you fled the village by hiding near the river; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you arrived near the location called Kodra e Zajmit, you saw a large number and one can say 100 of civilians between the road and Radishan; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: These civilians were not on the road. They were outside the road, if you can put the question clearly to me, please. These civilians were on the fields, on Radishan's side.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And these civilians were armed with different sorts of weapons, with axes, rifles and so forth; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if I'm to say to you that the police made maximum efforts to prevent these civilians from coming nearer to the civilians of Ljuboten in order to avoid a massacre, this would be correct, right?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: The police committed the bloodshed. I didn't see the police preventing them from anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if I were to tell you that the police fired in the air in order to prevent these furious civilians from beating the civilians, this would also be correct, right?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: No. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, amidst those policemen who prevented these civilians from beating the locals from Ljuboten, was Ilija Sovkovski, from OVR Cair, right? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: When we were stopped at that check-point? I think you're not clear on this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did Ilija Sovkovski, together with other policemen, prevented the civilians from beating or attacking the civilians from Ljuboten who were moving along that road?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You testified that you were taken to the Butel, or Cair, police station; is that correct? And that then you saw a large number of civilians carrying Molotov cocktails and other types of weapons and the police actually stopped them from attacking you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: I don't understand you. If you could put a short and clear question to me, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the way to Butel, or Cair police station, you also saw a large group of civilians, hundreds of civilians, carrying Molotov cocktails and other weapons or instruments, and the police was making efforts to prevent them from attacking you; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: I saw them on the way, in the van. I didn't see them at the police station. I saw them on the way to the police station. I could see this through a hole in the van, where we were. These were civilians from Radishani; this I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the police station Butel, you -- your details were taken down and nobody maltreated you there; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: No, this is not correct. We were beaten with everything they could find, and I can still feel pain on my head due to those beatings by the police in the Butel police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In item 26 of your statement from October 2004 you said the following, first on item 25 you said the following. It refers to the Butel police station. "[In English] To a cell in the basement of the station. It was normal cell and there were some other people in the cell when we arrived. Finally we were some 50 or 60 people in the cell and I remember that there was another cell full of the people as well." Interpretation in item 26 you said: "[In English] Cell for more than 3 hours and during this time, we were not beaten or kicked at. Some of my relatives were in my cell; some in the other one." [Interpretation] What you said before and -- differs from what you are saying today. Is that correct, Mr. Rexhepi?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: I told you the following. When -- on the way to the Butel police station they beat us, then they put us in a cell. They beat us there as well and while they were bringing other people, maybe they stopped beating us for one hour or two hours and then they resumed. It was a room with 50 or 60 people in it. Some were beaten more than others.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But, anyway, this differs from what you said to the investigator in October 2004. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: I don't know how well you understand me. I'm telling you what is in my statement. And I'm telling you what actually happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that at the Karpos police station a paraffin test was performed and that it came out positive?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: This is not true. I was not subjected to this paraffin test. They went -- they wanted me to sign. I lifted my hand and then one of the policemen hit me on the head with his gun-barrel and that's where I fainted.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could exhibit 55 be shown to the witness, please. N002, P50 N002-0084-108. English version, ET-N002-0191-1.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rexhepi, on the upper left-hand corner you can see that it writes Republic of Macedonia, Ministry of Interior, criminalistic police. There is a number of the document and the date, 14th of August, 2001. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the middle of the document it writes: Subject, analysis of traces of nitrite particles. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The first paragraph says: "Regarding your letter with the aforementioned number requesting to be determined whether on the submitted pieces of foils with which traces for gunpowder tests were taken from the hands of Qamuran Rexhepi, there are gunpowder particles present. We would like to inform you of the following. Using the identification reagent for nitrites, diphenylamine, analysis of the submitted foils has been performed. The reaction used was positive on the foil of the right hand on the aforementioned person." Does this document refer to you, Mr. Rexhepi?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: My name is mentioned in this document. But this is not true.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You agree with me that in this -- at that day all the people who did not have a positive test were released and sent home?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: You mean for the others who didn't test positive? Yes. Those were, but we didn't test positive either, and I wonder how can they test positive or we test positive and they don't when we were all together.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rexhepi, you testified that after that you were taken to court; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The persons that took you to the court behaved well with you, and you were even offered something to drink; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in the court, no one mistreated you; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: The person who took me there, no; but those from Bit Pazar police station, yes. They wanted to beat me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you earlier, Mr. Rexhepi, you did not mention to the Prosecutor the persons that were from the Bit Pazar police station; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Which persons do you mean? Those who took me there were from Karpos.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But until yesterday, until before the preparations for this hear -- testifying, you never mentioned that had you had seen people from the Bit Pazar police station. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement from October 2004 in item 32 you testified as follows: "[In English] Brought me to the station were active police officer and they even asked me if I would like to have something to drink or eat. They didn't beat me at all but I could see that the others were being brought to the court by police officer wearing mask and the mask men maltreated everybody they brought to the court." [Interpretation] Is this what you testified in 2004?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you only saw then some people wearing masks. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: I saw them in court. In court, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that is exactly the opposite from what you stated today. That there you saw and recognised the persons from the police station Bit Pazar. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. Please put it clearly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What you said to the Prosecutor's investigator in October 2004 that you have seen only some people wearing masks, beating people brought in is completely different from what you stated before this Court, when you said that you recognised the policemen from the police station Bit Pazar. Is that correct that these two statements are different, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Please more clearly and shorter questions, please. I can't understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rexhepi, I kindly ask you just to answer with yes or a no: Is what you stated to the Prosecutor in 2004 different from what you have given as a testimony today before this Court?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: I didn't call these persons -- I didn't -- I didn't report these persons at that time because I was afraid. I reported them now.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You were interviewed by an investigating judge; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: I didn't hear the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you entered the courtroom, you were interrogated by an investigating judge; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the prosecutor, Vilma Ruskovska was there, as well as your attorney, Fidovski Tahir; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were then informed about your rights, and after you gave your statement you signed it; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Once again, please. I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After you gave the statement to the investigating judge, you signed it personally.

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask that the witness is shown a part of the P52 exhibit that is at the same time part of the Exhibit P50 but in order to facilitate the displaying of the document we have scanned it as 65 ter 1D458, 1D4238. Considering that this document was not translated, we then organised for a draft, a working translation. The translation is 1D4239. 4238 is Macedonian and 4239 is English. Mr. Rexhepi, you see the document issued by the investigating judge of the Basic Court Skopje II, Jovan Lazarevski which appoints to you a ex officio counsel on the date of 14th of August, 2001. The counsel Fidovski Tahir is appointed for you. Can you see that document?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the statement of 2004 in item 33, you stated the following: "[In English] After one hour I was taken into an office. There was a lawyer appointed by the court, but I said I don't want to have any lawyers. The judge insisted that I must have one." [Interpretation] Did you state this to the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: I didn't want a lawyer. No, this is not true. I didn't have a lawyer at that time. I didn't have a private -- a personal lawyer. It was the state that gave us a lawyer, that provided a lawyer to us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So if I understood well, you did have an attorney appointed for you by the court, and it is not correct, as you said before, that you did not have a defence counsel?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I seek to tender this document that I indicated a decision for an ex officio defence counsel appointment as Defence exhibit, since it was indeed part of P50, but this is a part that is not translated, and in accordance with the agreement with the Prosecutor, if within a large bundle of documents there are some documents which were not translated by the Prosecutor, there is an agreement that we could tender those documents as our own exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is will be exhibit 1D102.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And is it correct, Mr. Rexhepi, that your wife, Gjusler -- is that the name of your wife?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Could you state the name more clearly?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Gjusler Rexhepi.

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Yes. Gjusler.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Gjusler, I apologise. I apologise for mispronouncing. Is it correct that your wife has chosen an attorney for you, apart from this ex officio appointed attorney and actually those were the attorneys Numan Limani and Slobodan Bogojevic. Are you aware of this fact?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: No. I have a father and a mother. My wife cannot go out and search for a lawyer for me. I don't want such questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will ask that the witness is shown 65 ter 1D457, Macedonian 1D4236, English 1D4237. Mr. Rexhepi, do you see the document composed by the attorney Numan Limani on the 16th of August, 2001, and this is a power of attorney document signed by your wife giving to Mr. Numan Limani and Slobodan Bogojevic, attorneys from Skopje, the right to represent you. Is that power of attorney certificate that was signed by your wife?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: This is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, considering the document I have in front of me, I would seek to tender it as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, there will be exhibit number 1D103.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true, Mr. Rexhepi, that later you and several of the other accused selected Dragan Vasilevski to be your attorney and he represented you in the further course of the procedure?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: While I was in prison someone came to ask me but he didn't say whether he was an attorney or else. He just came to ask me whether I was okay and that's all. He asked me nothing else. I don't know. I didn't take an attorney to defend me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you then authorised this attorney and he wrote a motion challenging the form of the indictment against you, and you were then together appearing before the court. In October 2001, you appeared before the trial chamber?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: They took us to the court and returned us back after 10 to 15 minutes. We didn't speak anything there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you were released from the remand prison when the president Boris Trajkovski pardoned you, you never pressed charges against any of the persons who allegedly ill-treated you during this period; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: Once again, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You never filed a criminal report against anyone who ill-treated you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: No, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You never asked your attorney to do it your behalf; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: I didn't have a lawyer. Whom could I complain to?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You never wanted to talk to the Macedonian police; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You discussed the events which had taken place only with the international representatives, and you never wanted to give a statement to the police; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: I didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that you never went to the police or to the court to report any of the persons or to discuss with the police what has happened to you.

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You did not trust the Macedonian police and this is why you only discussed about these things with the representatives of the international organisations and this Tribunal; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMURAN REXHEPI
utterances.text: I don't trust the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have concluded my cross-examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Clearly, we can't continue and finish today. So we must adjourn and we resume on Monday at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 16th day of July, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.45 p.m.,
